reason: The +0.0141 ceiling counts all 1,907 a_never FN edges, but a standalone rescue track can reach only a small part of them. (1) The 1,567 missed GT nodes form 721 runs: 370 of length 1 and about 290 of length 2-4 (744 nodes). Only about 453 nodes sit in runs of 5 or more, 160 of them in runs of 10 or more (wf_ideas_v2/r1_hyp_detection.notes.md). 846 of the 1,907 FN edges lie inside runs; about 1,061 are boundary edges (r1_verify_gate-aware-refine-head_arithmetic.notes.md). A new component that is not attached to the existing track leaves every boundary edge FN, and min_track_len 6 removes all runs shorter than 6. The internal edges of runs of 6 or more number about 300 FN, a ceiling of about +0.0022 lab. (2) Only about 424 of the 1,567 missed nodes have no raw peak within 10 um. 58% have a confident peak 7-10 um away, and the valley test on 326 of them found an intensity valley in only 4%. So most a_never are the same blob, off by an annotation offset or axial elongation. Long runs are the persistent per-track offset case (dz sign agrees 82%; predecessor 7.8 um away), and a DoG peak there falls within 6.5 um of our node, so clearance rejects it. The reachable pool is about 90-150 FN, a ceiling of +0.0007..+0.0011 lab. (3) Several gates compound on these nodes: DoG recall on dim, z-blurred nuclei; the 6.5 um clearance, since the missed GT's nearest node is at a median of about 7.2 um in 44b6; the valley gate, which passes only about 44% of true targets; clearance required in every frame; 1-frame gaps; and the 3 um border exclusion, although misses are enriched at z<=3 slices and at xy borders. Recall comes to about 0.3-0.6, so the gross gain is +0.0002..+0.0007 lab. Nodes from unannotated misses and junk cost -0.0002..-0.0014 (+1% nodes = -0.00093, T_true is fixed). Net lab is about -0.001..+0.0005, and the pre-registered +0.002 gate fails with P ~0.9. (4) Transfer: the public edge term is about 0.914 against about 0.902 in the lab, so the public detector's recall is close to the lab's, not to LOEO's 0.86. The public truly-absent pool is guessed at 1-3x the lab's, giving a public gain of +0.000..+0.0015. That is below the +0.002 bar and inside the 0.003 LB noise. (5) The idea's arithmetic leaves out one risk. With clearance 6.5 um below the 7 um matching gate, a new node can take a GT node that an old node matches at more than 3.25 um. About 7.9k GT nodes sit in the 4-7 um swap zone, so the change can create FN/FP swaps.
fix_if_any: Do not build the kernel patch first. Run a 1-hour desk test on friend A's cache (exp39 tails + raw zarr; the DoG code is CPU only). For the 1,567 a_never nodes, measure: (a) the share with a DoG maximum within 3 um that has clearance >= 6.5 um from every final node; (b) how many such peaks chain into tracks of 6 or more that cover GT runs, counting only internal edges; (c) the added-node rate over all frames. Build only if (b) gives >= 150 FN at <= 0.5% nodes, i.e. a net lab gain of at least +0.0006. That is still under +0.002, so only a second change could make it pay: attach the DoG chains to the open ends of existing tracks, which also converts the ~1,061 boundary edges (ceiling x2-3). That is readmit/gapfill territory, LB-neutral in v2. Or use the DoG maxima as extra low-cost ILP candidates (linajea-style over-complete set), a larger re-run of the stack. The only setting with real headroom is LOEO-44b6 with the scratch detector (recall 0.86, about 8x the misses). Run there first: if the gain there is not >= +0.003, drop the idea.
realistic_public_gain: +0.000..+0.0015. Central guess +0.0005, below the +0.002 bar and inside the 0.003 LB noise. Worst case about -0.0014 if the 1.5% node cap fills with junk.
realistic_private_gain: +0.000..+0.002. Central guess about +0.0007: hidden embryos may miss more nuclei than the public one, but the per-track annotation-offset share and the standalone-track structure limit it the same way. Downside bounded at about -0.0014 by the cap.
